reminders.intro: When a contribution isn't paid by its due date, the system reminds the member, then brings in, ever closer, their circle and the community. The steps trigger by themselves when this page opens, until the server takes over; SMS and WhatsApp messages are prepared but don't go out yet, for lack of a sending service.
reminders.ladderHint: Delay is counted in days since the due date.

1.title: Automatic reminder
1.body: SMS and WhatsApp notification the day after the due date, then a reminder at D+3. Kind, factual message with the deadline to avoid penalties.

2.title: Financial Community Manager
2.body: The group's local Community Manager contacts the member by WhatsApp or phone, tries to understand and offers solutions: grace period, partial payment, amicable arrangement.

3.title: Mentor-sponsor
3.body: The mentor-sponsor is alerted. Their commission depends on their sponsored members' reputation: they step in as moral guarantor and local mediator.

4.title: Joint guarantee
4.body: The other group members are informed and can cover the contribution together (e.g. 1/35 each in a group of 36), the member repaying with penalties.

5.title: Reserve Fund
5.body: If the guarantee isn't enough, the DBC Reserve Fund steps in so the cycle isn't blocked. The debt is entered in the audit trail and a repayment plan is written down.

items.question: How is the payout calculated?
items.answer: Every member of the group contributes the same amount each month, based on their DBC level. A group has 36 people: each month, 3 of them receive the pot of their level.

items.question: How is the payout order decided?
items.answer: The order is set when the cycle starts, for all 12 rounds of the year: 3 members receive the pot each month, and each member receives it exactly once per cycle, on their turn.

items.question: What happens if I miss a month?
items.answer: Your turn isn't affected, but the group can still see that you're behind (see the contribution tracking below) until you catch up.

items.question: What happens once all 12 rounds are done?
items.answer: The cycle is closed: you can then restart a new tontine at this level or request to move up to the next level, from the button at the bottom of this page.

guide.subtitle: A good interview lasts 10 to 15 minutes. It checks that the candidate understood the tontine, can contribute every month and is joining the DBC for the right reasons.

before.title: Before the interview
items: Open the candidate's file and re-read their occupation, city, sponsor and chosen tontine.
Read the administration's message, if there is one.
Write to them with the WhatsApp button: the message is ready, you suggest a time to talk.
You have {{days}} days from receiving the file to submit your report.

during.title: During the conversation
during.intro: Stay simple and friendly, like a real conversation. A few useful questions:
items: Can you tell me what you do today, and what you would like to build?
How did you hear about the DBC, and what made you want to join us?
How does the tontine work in your view? (monthly contribution, pot in your turn)
Are you comfortable paying this amount every month without getting into difficulty?
Do you have any questions or concerns?

verify.title: What to check
verify.intro: These are the 5 points of the report:
items: They understand how the tontine works.
They commit to the monthly contribution.
Their professional project is clear.
What they say matches their registration (city, occupation, sponsor).
Their motivation is sincere.

after.title: After the conversation: the report
after.intro: Come back to the platform, in the candidate's file. Nothing to write: everything is ticked.
items: Tick how the conversation went (WhatsApp, call or in person).
Say whether you reached the candidate. If not, choose “Unreachable”: you can try again.
Rate each point: Yes, Medium or No. Tick the warning signs, if any.
Add a one-line note if needed, then click “Positive interview” or “Not conclusive”. The buttons stay greyed out until the report is filled in.
For “Not conclusive”, tick at least one reason: the administration will see it. You have {{days}} days to submit everything; after that, the administration is notified.

tips.title: Good habits
items: Be warm and patient, and stay respectful.
Never promise a gain or a pot date.
Never ask for money during the interview.
If in doubt, tick “Medium”: the administration will decide.
A candidate who does not answer? Try again another day before marking them unreachable.

diaspo-fund.name: DBC Diaspo Fund
diaspo-fund.summary: Diaspora members co-invest in projects back home.
diaspo-fund.overview:
The DBC Diaspo Fund lets members living abroad pool their resources to finance projects back home.
Instead of investing alone and from a distance, everyone co-invests with other members of the community, in projects chosen together.

points.2: Support concrete projects in the country
points.3: Invest together rather than alone and from afar

diaspo-fund.audience: Diaspora members who want to invest in their home country.

export-import.name: Export-Import Club
export-import.summary: Trade opportunities between members from different countries.
export-import.overview:
The Export-Import Club connects members from different countries who want to trade products and services.
It turns the community into a business network: a member who produces, sells or wants to buy can find a partner among the other members.

points.1: Find business partners within the community
points.2: Trade between members from different countries
points.3: Rely on the trust of the DBC network

export-import.audience: Merchant, producer and entrepreneur members who want to grow their trade across borders.

joint-ventures.name: Joint-Venture Projects
joint-ventures.summary: Shared projects between members, supervised by DBC.
joint-ventures.overview:
A joint venture brings two or more members together around a shared project: they pool their means, skills and work.
DBC supervises these projects to keep a clear framework between partners.

points.1: Team up with other members around a project
points.3: Move forward within a framework supervised by DBC

joint-ventures.audience: Members who have a project, or skills to put at the service of a project carried with others.

real-estate.name: Communal Real Estate
real-estate.summary: A shared land and property initiative.
real-estate.overview:
Communal Real Estate lets members invest together in land and property.
What you could not always acquire alone, you can acquire with others, within the community.

points.1: Invest in land and property together
points.2: Access assets that are hard to acquire alone

real-estate.audience: Members who want to invest in property without doing it alone.

invest-back-home.name: Invest Back Home
invest-back-home.summary: Local investment as a way to prepare your return.
invest-back-home.overview:
Invest Back Home is for members who plan to return home one day.
The idea is to invest locally now, to prepare your return and arrive with solid foundations already in place.

points.2: Prepare your return step by step
points.3: Arrive with foundations already in place

consulting.summary: A consulting agency for community businesses.

tontine-royale.summary: Rotating collective savings — 12 months · 36 members min · Capital + Passive income.

Members contribute every month and the pot is paid out in turn, over a 12-month cycle bringing together at least 36 members. It combines building capital with passive income.

admin.title: Understanding the tontine and the register

cycle.title: One group, 12 rounds
cycle.text: A group brings together 36 members. Every month, 3 of them receive the pot: within 12 months, everyone has had a turn.
cycle.hint: Tap a round to see which members receive the pot that month.

money.title: Contribute 12 times, receive one pot
money.text: Each member contributes every month for 12 months. When their turn comes, they receive the pot: 11 net contributions, because the 1st one covers the annual registration fee.
money.hint: Switch level to see the matching amounts.

auto.title: Administration approves nothing
auto.text: A contribution shows as paid as soon as it is received. There is no “approve” button and no “mark as paid out”: the register updates by itself.
auto.hint: Simulate a payment arriving and watch the row change.

ledger.title: Reading the ledger
ledger.text: One row per member, one column per month. The cells show the state of each contribution at a glance, and the totals at the bottom give what is still outstanding.
ledger.hint: Tap a state in the legend to highlight the matching cells.

journal.title: The journal: everything, by date
journal.text: Every transaction in date order, like an account book: what is received, what is paid out, and what was not paid. Totals are at the bottom.
journal.hint: Filter by transaction type and watch the totals recalculate.

statement.title: A member's account statement
statement.text: Click a name to open their statement: what they contributed, the pot received and the running balance. The balance stays negative until the pot is paid out: that is normal.
statement.hint: Step through the lines and watch the balance change.

admin.intro: Scroll down to move along the road: each step comes alive with a small demo you can play with.
admin.doneText: The register holds no more secrets. The tour stays available and can be replayed at any time.

tontinePriority.title: How the payout order is decided
tontinePriority.intro: The order in which the members of a group receive the pot is not chosen: the platform calculates it with the DBC Priority Score (SPD), a mark out of 100 points spread over 5 criteria.
tontinePriority.sixMonths: A new member cannot receive the pot during their first {{months}} months in the community: their turn is placed at the first possible month.

urgency.name: Verified and documented urgency
urgency.how: A real, verified and documented need. The Governance Committee validates each urgency within 72 h; proofs are uploaded in the app and kept in the audit trail.
urgency.footnote: An urgency not validated by the Committee earns no points.

regularity.name: Payment regularity
regularity.how: Calculated automatically by the platform from the payment history. No input, no evaluation deadline: it cannot be edited and everything is kept in the audit trail.
regularity.footnote: A settled payment does not erase the delay: it stays counted.

coins.name: Community engagement (DBC Coins)
coins.how: Read automatically by the platform from the member's journal and activities. No input, no evaluation deadline.
coins.footnote: A member who is too recent has nothing to evaluate yet: the box stays empty (—). To earn Coins: completed training +50, referral +100, monthly challenge +75, DBC event +50, public testimonial +30, and other actions.

level.name: Seniority and DBC level
level.how: Read automatically by the platform from the member's journal: registration date and level reached. No input, no evaluation deadline.
level.footnote: During the first 2 months in the community the box stays empty (—): probation period.

recommendation.name: Mentor-sponsor recommendation
recommendation.how: The mentor-sponsor rates their mentee from 0 to 10 on four qualities; the average gives the points. They have 72 h to submit their rating, with automatic reminders at 24 h, 48 h and 66 h.
recommendation.footnote: With no rating within 72 h, the criterion takes its default value (3 points). A veto only counts if it is justified in writing and recognised as valid by the Governance Committee.

productive.label: Documented productive investment
productive.detail: Professional equipment, stock, premises: quote or pro-forma validated by the Governance Committee.
productive.proof: Quote or pro-forma for the equipment, stock or premises.

debt.label: Repayment of a debt at immediate risk
debt.detail: Workshop rent overdue, critical supplier. Proof required.
debt.proof: Proof of the debt (reminder, contract, unpaid invoice).

opportunity.label: Business opportunity with a verifiable deadline
opportunity.detail: Call for tenders, customer order with deposit, certifying training on a fixed date. Purchase order or summons required.
opportunity.proof: Purchase order, summons or call-for-tenders notice.

social.label: Urgent non-productive need
social.detail: School fees, uncovered medical costs. Proof required.
social.proof: Proof of the costs (invoice, school certificate, medical quote).

rated.label: Average of the sponsor's ratings
rated.detail: Points = the rounded average, from 0 to 10.

veto.label: Justified veto
veto.detail: At least one member objects in writing, and the Governance Committee recognises the reason as valid.

publication.title: Published from the first month
publication.text: The full ranking is calculated, validated by the Executive Committee and published from the first month. Each member receives a notification with their rank, the expected date of receipt and the expected amount. It is the law of the group.

topScores.title: The first 3 months go to the best scores
topScores.text: The pots of months 1, 2 and 3 go to the highest SPD scores.

ends.title: Mentor-sponsor and Local Community Manager at the end
ends.text: The group's mentor-sponsor receives second to last, the Local Community Manager last.

swap.title: Voluntary rank swap
swap.text: Two members can swap ranks. The swap is formalised in the app, digitally co-signed by both, validated by the Governance Committee and recorded in the audit trail. It is final and irrevocable.

tie.title: Tied scores
tie.text: The administration chooses each member's place among tied members.

recalc.title: Score recalculated every cycle
recalc.text: The score is not frozen for life: it is recalculated at each new cycle.

bylaws.title: The internal rules prevail
bylaws.text: The internal rules, signed by everyone at the start of the cycle, prevail over everything in case of dispute.
